sana: FYI i ran into a weird tail on cold-starts for a customer using long-system prompts. the initial kv fetch pulls ~50 shards but only ~6 layers are hot for the first tokens. wondering if we should introduce a tiny 'hotmap probe' step that asks the bundle for a compact map of hot ranges before deciding what to stream.
diego: sounds useful. we already have some per-model telemetry that records layer access heatmaps but it's coarse. hard question: where does the map live? in the bundle manifest, a sidecar object, or a registry?
li: prefer sidecar file inside bundle (e.g., .hotmap) so private deployments get the info locally. sidecar payload should be tiny, just bitsets or run-length encoded ranges per shard. no prompts or raw traces.
sana: agree on RLE. example sidecar sketch: ```
# hotmap sidecar (textproto-ish)
model: "example-v1"
shard 0: runs=0..3,8..9
shard 1: runs=0..2
shard 5: runs=4..7
version: "2026-03-20"
```
diego: good. runtime flow idea: router or prefetcher calls `GET /bundle/:id/hotmap` (fast cached) then chooses between 1) micro-prefetch shard-layer ranges, 2) index-first no-prefetch, or 3) hybrid (preload shard headers + selective chunks).
li: we must ensure hotmap lookup is non-blocking for SLOs. always fallback to index-first if lookup latency > 5ms. also add TTLs so nodes don't hammer registry.
sana: policy: only use hotmap when bundle reports expected savings > 10ms and overhead < 20kb prefetch. else skip. we should capture these thresholds in the manifest metadata.
diego: what about dynamic melts (hotness changes after fine-tuning)? We need a version field on hotmap and a simple invalidation protocol. sidecar should include `hotmap_version` and `observed_at`. nodes check version and prefer newer ones.
li: telemetry: `hotmap_lookup` (hit/miss), `hotmap_version`, `hotmap_prefetch_bytes`, `hotmap_latency_gain_ms`, and `hotmap_misprediction_penalty_ms`. also `hotmap_source` (bundle-sidecar/registry).
sana: ops note: limit concurrent hotmap-driven prefetches per node to X KB/s to avoid IO storms. add a circuit-breaker: if misprediction rate > 30% for a bucket, disable it automatically.
diego: security/privacy: never store prompt-derived fingerprints in the bundle. If we want mapping from prompt-features to hotmap IDs, store only hashed buckets in the tenant registry and make that optional per-tenant. private installs default to local-only matching.
li: implementation tasks: 1) define .hotmap sidecar format (RLE or compact bitset), 2) add optional manifest metadata `hotmap_enabled:true/false`, `hotmap_bytes_estimate`, `hotmap_version`, 3) runtime: non-blocking lookup + best-effort prefetch + circuit-breaker, 4) telemetry fields above.
sana: i'll draft a tiny RFC and include a microbenchmark plan. diego you can prototype the client-side prefetch heuristics?
diego: yes i'll hack a PoC that reads .hotmap and runs A/B on staging. rough guess: for chat-like flows we might save 15-50ms median first-token, but bad maps can add 10-30ms tail. need to tune.
infra-bot: ticket created: ENGML-2042 "hotmap-sidecar-rfc" assigned to sana/diego.
li: one more thought: unify this with existing warmup_profiles idea but keep names distinct: hotmap=static per-bundle heat fingerprint; warmup_profiles=fingerprint->profile mapping. both can coexist.
sana: nice. will include compatibility notes in RFC. thanks.
